title: Career Roadmap: Data Analyst
summary: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, analyses and interprets data to help organisations make informed business decisions. Students from Economics and Finance backgrounds can use their understanding of markets, financial performance and economic trends to solve business problems through data.

about.label: Primary Industries
about.text: Banking, Finance, Consulting, E-commerce, Technology, Healthcare

about.label: Suitable For
about.text: Students who enjoy numbers, business problem-solving, statistics, research and interpreting data

blocks.text: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, analyses and interprets data to help organisations make informed business decisions. Students from Economics and Finance backgrounds can use their understanding of markets, financial performance and economic trends to solve business problems through data.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Collect and clean data from spreadsheets, databases and business systems.
Analyse revenue, expenses, customer behaviour and financial performance.
Build dashboards and reports using Power BI or Tableau.
Write SQL queries to retrieve and summarise data.
Use statistics to identify patterns, trends and anomalies.
Communicate findings to management and business teams.
Translate business questions into measurable insights and recommendations.

blocks.label: Example
blocks.text: A bank wants to understand why loan applications are being rejected. A Data Analyst studies application data, identifies common patterns and presents findings to the credit and business teams.
Undergraduate route
BS in Economics
Build knowledge of econometrics, statistics, economic indicators, quantitative methods and research.
BS in Finance
Develop financial analysis, accounting, financial modelling, business performance measurement and investment fundamentals.
Technical specialisation
Add SQL, Excel, Python, data visualisation and statistical analysis to the degree's business and quantitative foundation.
Further study options
Depending on career goals and admission eligibility, consider:

items.text: MSc Data Analytics
MSc Business Analytics
MSc Economics with Econometrics
MSc Statistics or Applied Statistics
MSc Financial Analytics
MBA in Business Analytics, particularly for later management-oriented roles

blocks.text: A postgraduate degree is not mandatory for many entry-level Data Analyst positions. Practical skills, projects and internships can also establish job readiness.
Year 1 — Business and Data Foundations

items.text: Strengthen mathematics, statistics and quantitative reasoning.
Learn Excel formulas, sorting, filtering, pivot tables and charts.
Understand basic accounting, economics and business terminology.
Practise data interpretation and structured problem-solving.

blocks.label: Mini-project
blocks.text: Analyse a sample household budget or monthly expense dataset.
Year 2 — SQL and Visualisation

items.text: Learn SQL, including SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, subqueries and window functions.
Study descriptive statistics, correlation and hypothesis testing.
Learn Power BI or Tableau.
Practise cleaning datasets and defining business metrics.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Build a sales dashboard showing revenue, profit, product performance and monthly trends.
Year 3 — Python and Business Analytics

items.text: Learn Python, pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib.
Study regression, time-series analysis and exploratory data analysis.
Work with financial, economic or customer datasets.
Practise communicating insights to non-technical audiences.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Analyse inflation, interest rates or company financial performance and explain the business implications.
Final Year — Portfolio and Job Preparation

items.text: Complete two or three substantial end-to-end analytics projects.
Build a portfolio using Power BI dashboards, SQL scripts and Python notebooks.
Apply for data analytics, business intelligence and financial analytics internships.
Practise SQL assessments, Excel tasks, statistics and case-study interviews.
Prepare a resume that highlights measurable project outcomes and business recommendations.

blocks.text: Adapt this plan to the actual duration and curriculum of the student's degree.

blocks.label: Recommended learning order
blocks.text: Excel → SQL → Power BI → statistics → Python. Students can adjust the order based on their existing skills and the requirements of their target roles.

Customer and Marketing Data Analyst

Create a portfolio that demonstrates the complete analytical process: defining a question, preparing data, analysing it, visualising results and recommending action.

blocks.text: Students can look for opportunities in banks, financial services, consulting firms, fintech companies, retail, e-commerce and technology organisations.
For each project, include the business question, data source, cleaning steps, analysis, dashboard or visualisations, key findings and limitations. Use public, synthetic or properly authorised data.
Consider these options based on the skills you want to demonstrate:

items.text: Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst (PL-300): for Power BI data preparation, modelling, visualisation and reporting.
Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate: for introductory analytics workflows and practical projects.
IBM Data Analyst Professional Certificate: for foundational data analysis and programming skills.

Undergraduate student → Analytics internship or project experience
Entry level
Junior Data Analyst / Reporting Analyst / MIS Analyst
Experienced level
Data Analyst / Business Intelligence Analyst / Financial Data Analyst
Advanced stage
Senior Data Analyst / Analytics Lead / Analytics Manager
With additional study and experience, some professionals transition into data science, product analytics, financial analytics or analytics consulting.

Self-service business intelligence

Decision intelligence and business experimentation

blocks.text: AI tools can speed up SQL writing, coding and report preparation, but analysts still need to verify calculations, understand data quality, protect sensitive information and interpret results correctly.

Final Recommendation
For students pursuing a BS in Economics or Finance, Data Analyst is a practical career pathway that combines existing business knowledge with technical and statistical skills.

Prioritise Excel, SQL, Power BI, statistics and Python, and use economics or finance datasets to build a specialised portfolio. This helps distinguish the student from candidates who know analytics tools but cannot connect their findings to business decisions.
